Preparation, protection, and clean finish transitions

Interior painting that respects the room around it.

A professional interior finish depends on surface repair, preparation, protection, product choice, application, and clean transitions at trim, cabinets, ceilings, and adjacent materials.

Request a consultation Explore design ideas
Call (206) 407-6291
Completed RT project pictured · Redmond

Project fit

The service covers residential walls, ceilings, trim, doors, and qualifying cabinet-painting scopes as standalone work or part of a larger renovation.

Typical scope

  • Surface review, repair, sanding, priming, and caulking
  • Protection of floors, fixtures, furniture, and adjacent rooms
  • Walls, ceilings, trim, doors, and millwork
  • Cabinet painting and refinishing preparation
  • Color, sheen, product, ventilation, and cure-time planning

Preparation

Treat the surface before asking paint to hide it.

Patching, sanding, caulking, stain blocking, cleaning, and primer selection affect how the final coating looks and lasts.

Protection and dust control are planned around the occupied home.

Cabinet painting

Use a cabinet-specific preparation and coating process.

Cabinet painting requires cleaning, disassembly, labeling, abrasion, repair, primer, coating, cure time, and careful reassembly.

It remains part of Interior Painting at launch and may become a separate page when proof and demand support it.

Finish detail

Control sheen, edges, coverage, and transitions.

Trim, doors, walls, ceilings, built-ins, and hardware all meet in visible places.

Product and application choices should reflect light, cleaning needs, use, and the condition of each substrate.

How the work moves

A process that keeps decisions ahead of construction.

Discovery and site assessment

We clarify goals, review existing conditions, identify constraints, and determine what needs deeper investigation before a scope is written.

Design and pre-construction

Layout, materials, trade requirements, permits, allowances, schedule factors, and decision deadlines are coordinated into one buildable plan.

Construction and completion

The work is sequenced, protected, inspected, communicated, and closed out with a final walkthrough and documented completion items.

Budget and schedule orientation

Scope the variables before suggesting a number.

Useful early guidance identifies what changes the investment and timeline. A responsible project range follows an assessment of the property, scope, finish expectations, and delivery constraints.

Common factors

  • Existing structural and mechanical conditions
  • Project size, layout changes, and finish level
  • Permit, engineering, and design requirements
  • Material availability and product lead times
  • Site access, protection, and project sequencing

Questions homeowners ask

Interior Painting FAQs

Is cabinet painting included?

Yes, as a dedicated Interior Painting subsection at launch. The scope depends on cabinet material, condition, existing coating, desired finish, and access.

What preparation is typically required?

Preparation may include cleaning, repair, sanding, caulking, stain blocking, priming, masking, and protection based on the surface.

Can painting be coordinated with flooring or remodeling?

Yes. Sequencing paint with cabinetry, flooring, trim, electrical work, and final punch items helps prevent damage and duplicated protection.
